### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Include workflowId in the header will enable the api gateway/frontend route the workflow request to correct active cluster without having to decode/open the request payload

### Describe the solution you'd like
Workflow requests are requests for a specific workflow, i.e. StartWorkflow, RespondWorkflow/Activity, SignalWorkflow etc.

For actions initiated from the SDK (e.g., StartWorkflow, SignalWorkflow, TerminateWorkflow), the SDK needs to add the workflowId to the request header.

For action-after-poll requests (i.e., RespondWorkflow/ActivityTask), SDK only needs to attach the header from the matching poll response to the following API calls.

### Additional context

server will add header at the poll response

PoC of how this might work:

* https://github.com/cretz/temporal-api/commit/fe8c062341dc43c7747fd13816cbdb1aa5014947 - API changes for adding the annotation and using it
* https://github.com/cretz/temporal-api-go/commit/d43d11d83b42eb29d2bee12dcad934eabc0166e8 - Code generated utility to extract headers for Go (would have one in Java, TS, and Rust)
* https://github.com/cretz/temporal-sdk-go/commit/e75bb9adc39415fe3604139a718e70dba1a5bba7 - Applying of the utility in Go

Not as confident that every RPC should have to opt-out of the annotation here, but that doesn't have to be decided to develop the feature if we decide we want this feature

Also, I have adjusted the title to reflect a more general nature, and we have acknowledged the following:

* This is an optional optimization header that is not required by clients and does not affect behavior from a user-POV
* Server side does not trust this header implicitly, the request body is the true source of information about the resource

title: Add resource ID to the http header for API requests
